from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems", [
            "Systems represent intersections of geometric objects.",
            "Solutions are the specific meeting points.",
            "Matrices act as linear transformations.",
            "Visualizing movement clarifies algebraic results.",
            "Linear algebra links geometry and computation."
        ])
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1], x_length=5, y_length=4)

        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a 2D plane with lines #FF5733 (Line A) and #33FF57 (Line B).

        line_b = axes.plot(lambda x: x - 1, color="#33FF57")
        self.play(Create(line_a), Create(line_b), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the intersection point #FFFF33
        intersection = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 1), color="#FFFF33", radius=0.1)
        intersection_label = Text("(2, 1)", font_size=20, color="#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(intersection_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(intersection), FadeIn(intersection_label), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF33"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate a vector #33A1FF moving from origin to intersection point.
        vector = Vector(axes.c2p(2, 1), color="#33A1FF")
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33A1FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Inverse Matrices: The 'Undo' Button", [
            "Inverse matrices reverse linear transformations.",
            "They act like undo buttons for space.",
            "Applying A then inverse restores original points."
        ])

        # Assets
        btn_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/button.svg"
        
        # Animation Setup
        vector_orig = Vector([1, 0.5], color="#FF5733")
        matrix_a = MathTex(r"A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}", color="#FFFFFF")
        matrix_inv = MathTex(r"A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 0.5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 \end{pmatrix}", color="#33FF57")
        
        button_a = SVGMobject(btn_asset)
        button_inv = SVGMobject(btn_asset)
        
        # Apply mandatory layout fixes (VideoCritic requests)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_a, 'A2', 'C3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_orig, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(button_a, 'A1', 'C1', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        vector_trans = vector_orig.copy().scale(2)
        vector_trans.set_color("#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a), FadeIn(button_a), FadeIn(vector_orig))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.place_in_area(matrix_inv, 'A4', 'C5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(button_inv, 'A6', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_inv), FadeIn(button_inv))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        vector_final = vector_orig.copy()
        
        # Visualize restoration
        self.play(Transform(vector_orig, vector_trans))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(vector_orig, vector_final), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Inverses exist when space is preserved.", "No crushing ensures perfect reconstruction.", "These concepts unify linear systems theory."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements

        self.play(
            FadeOut(concepts),
            FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)),

outline.topic: Linear Algebra: From Geometry to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce a system of equations as the intersection of lines (in 2D) or planes (in 3D). Visualize the solution as the specific point where these geometric objects meet. Introduce the prerequisite concept: A matrix acts as a linear transformation.
sections.example: Imagine two robots (Line A and Line B) moving on a 2D plane. Their paths are defined by 2x + y = 5 and x - y = 1. The solution is the exact coordinate (2, 1) where the robots collide.

sections.title: Inverse Matrices: The 'Undo' Button
sections.content: Explain that if a matrix transforms space, the inverse matrix reverses that transformation. Use a visual 'stretch/rotate' animation to show how applying A then A-inverse returns the point to its origin.
sections.example: A 'Scale-o-matic' device doubles the size of a cat image. The inverse matrix is the 'Shrink-o-matic' that brings the cat back to its original dimensions.

sections.title: Column Space: Where Can We Go?
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the column vectors. Visually represent this as the 'territory' reachable by combining the column vectors. If the vectors are independent, they cover a plane/space; if dependent, they collapse into a line.
sections.example: A scout dog can jump in two directions (Vector 1: North-East, Vector 2: South-East). The column space is the entire flat field the dog can reach by combining these two jump patterns.

sections.title: Null Space: What Gets Crushed?
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of all vectors that result in the zero vector when multiplied by A. Visually, this is the 'shadow' or the line/plane that gets squashed into a single point (the origin) during the transformation.
sections.example: A magical 'Flattening Lens' looks at a 3D forest. All trees standing exactly on a specific vertical line (the Null Space) are compressed into a single dot on the ground when viewed through the lens.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Connect the concepts: The existence of an inverse matrix implies the column space covers the entire output space and the null space contains only the zero vector (the 'no-crushing' condition).
sections.example: If our 'Flattening Lens' (Null Space) is empty, we can perfectly reconstruct the 3D forest from the 2D image using the Inverse Matrix.
